q: Under Clause 17B of the GCC (April-2022), Liquidated Damages (LD) for delay in completion of a railway work, where the delay exceeds 50% of the stipulated period, are levied at the rate of:

options.A: 0.1% of the contract value per week
options.B: 0.30% of the contract value per week
options.C: 1% of the contract value per week
options.D: 2% of the contract value per week

e: Clause 17B of the GCC April-2022 levies LD on graduated slabs - 0.01 to 0.05% per week up to 25% delay, 0.10% for 25-50% delay and 0.30% above 50% delay - subject to a total cap of 5% of the contract value; the old flat 0.5% per week with a 10% cap no longer applies to works contracts. (Source: GCC April-2022, Clause 17B (ACS-1 dated 14.07.2022), consolidated up to ACS-12; effective April 2022).

q: Under the GCC, the two-packet system of tendering is mandatory for tenders above:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 25 lakh
options.C: Rs 50 lakh
options.D: Rs 1 crore

e: For tenders above Rs 50 lakh, the technical/eligibility packet and the financial packet are invited separately, so that the financial bids are opened only of tenderers found technically acceptable.

q: One of the canons of financial propriety is that:

options.A: Expenditure should be incurred as quickly as possible to avoid lapse of grant
options.B: Every public officer should exercise the same vigilance in respect of expenditure from public moneys as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in respect of his own money
options.C: A subordinate authority may sanction expenditure benefiting itself
options.D: Allotments should be fully spent before 31st March in all cases

e: One of the canons of financial propriety is that the allowances granted to a Government servant to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that, on the whole, they are not a source of profit to him.

q: When a change in the scope or quantities of a contract is so large that it changes the entire character of the contract, it is called:

options.A: Variation
options.B: Vitiation of the contract
options.C: Deviation
options.D: Extra item

e: When a change in scope or quantities is so extensive that the contract loses its original identity and character, it is not a mere variation but a vitiation of the contract.

q: The measurements of work done by a contractor, which form the basis of payment, are recorded in the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Measurement Book
options.C: Liability Register
options.D: Contractor's Ledger

e: The Measurement Book is the prescribed record in which measurements of work actually executed are recorded by the Engineer; the contractor's bills for payment are prepared on the basis of these measurements.

q: Performance Guarantee is required to be submitted by:

options.A: Every tenderer along with the tender
options.B: The successful tenderer after issue of the Letter of Acceptance
options.C: The tender committee before opening of tenders
options.D: Only by contractors executing deposit works

e: The Performance Guarantee is furnished by the successful tenderer after the Letter of Acceptance is issued, as security for due performance of his obligations under the contract.

q: 'Deposit works' are works:

options.A: Executed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Executed by Railways for outside bodies, the cost being borne by those bodies
options.C: Executed departmentally without tenders
options.D: Executed only within railway colonies

e: In deposit works, the Railway executes the work on behalf of an outside body or person, and the entire cost of the work, including departmental charges, is borne by that body.

q: An 'umbrella work' means:

options.A: A work executed under a single contractor for the whole zone
options.B: A group of related works, generally along a section or route, combined and sanctioned as one work
options.C: A work of urgent nature sanctioned by the General Manager
options.D: A work costing less than the threshold of a detailed estimate

e: Several related works, generally along a section or route, are combined and sanctioned as a single umbrella work instead of being sanctioned piece by piece.

q: If there is an excess over the sanctioned estimate of a work due to a change in its scope or design, the change is termed as:

options.A: Material modification
options.B: Book adjustment
options.C: Re-appropriation
options.D: Token variation

e: An excess over the sanctioned estimate arising from a change in the scope or design of the work is a material modification, which alters the basis of the sanction and needs competent sanction.

q: Security Deposit for a work should ordinarily be received from the contractor within:

options.A: 7 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.B: 21 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.C: 30 days of the Letter of Acceptance
options.D: 60 days of the Letter of Acceptance

e: The contractor is required to deposit the security amount with the Railway within 21 days of the issue of the Letter of Acceptance, failing which action can be taken under the contract conditions.

q: The Works Register maintained for works expenditure is primarily used to:

options.A: Record the attendance of engineering staff
options.B: Watch the expenditure incurred on each work against its sanctioned estimate
options.C: Maintain the list of approved contractors
options.D: Record the movement of materials between depots

e: The Works Register is the basic record through which expenditure incurred on each work is watched against its sanctioned estimate, so that excesses over the estimate are noticed in time.

q: A Completion Report of a work is prepared:

options.A: Before the detailed estimate is sanctioned
options.B: Along with the tender documents
options.C: After completion of the work, comparing actual expenditure with the sanctioned estimate and explaining the variations
options.D: Only when the work is abandoned

e: A Completion Report is prepared after the work is finished; it compares the actual expenditure with the sanctioned estimate and explains the variations, excess or savings, under each head.

q: In works accounting, the Material-at-Site (MAS) account represents:

options.A: Materials issued for a work but not yet actually consumed or utilised on the work
options.B: Materials lying in the stores depot
options.C: Surplus materials returned by the contractor
options.D: Materials condemned and awaiting disposal

e: Materials issued for a work but not yet actually utilised on it are held under the Material-at-Site account; the work is debited on issue and credited as the materials are consumed.

q: The Liability Register maintained in connection with works expenditure records:

options.A: The names of defaulting contractors
options.B: Liabilities and commitments incurred but not yet paid or adjusted
options.C: The leave account of engineering staff
options.D: Assets created during the year

e: The Liability Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred in connection with works but not yet paid or adjusted, enabling a watch over outstanding obligations against a work.

q: The Fixed Asset Register (asset register) of the Railways contains:

options.A: Details of outstanding advances of staff
options.B: Details of sundry creditors
options.C: A record of loans taken from the market
options.D: Details of assets created, including their cost and location

e: The Fixed Asset Register is the record of assets created through capital expenditure, showing their details, cost and location, and is used for accounting and verification of railway assets.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Separate General Conditions of Contract (GCC) exist for Works contracts and for Services contracts.
2. A single common GCC governs both works contracts and services contracts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: separate General Conditions of Contract exist for works contracts and for services contracts. Statement 2 is false because the two are governed by distinct sets of conditions, not one common GCC.

q: The Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) submitted by unsuccessful tenderers is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.B: Converted into security deposit automatically
options.C: Refunded after finalisation of the tender
options.D: Adjusted against the first running bill of the successful tenderer

e: The earnest money of tenderers who do not succeed is refunded after the tender is finalised; it is neither forfeited nor converted into security deposit, which concerns only the successful tenderer.

q: Where negotiations with tenderers become unavoidable, they should be held:

options.A: With all the tenderers one by one
options.B: Only with the lowest (L1) tenderer
options.C: Only with the highest (H1) tenderer
options.D: With the tenderer recommended by the executive

e: Where negotiations become unavoidable, they are held only with the lowest (L1) tenderer; negotiating with other tenderers would vitiate the fairness and sanctity of the tender process.

q: The Price Variation Clause in a works contract provides for:

options.A: Extension of the completion period without levy of damages
options.B: Change in the scope of work ordered by the Engineer
options.C: Termination of the contract by either party
options.D: Adjustment of the contract price on account of variation in the prices of materials and labour during execution

e: The Price Variation Clause provides for adjustment of the contract price for variations in the prices of specified materials and labour during execution, in accordance with the prescribed formula.

q: Disputes arising out of a works contract, which cannot be settled amicably between the Railway and the contractor, are resolved through:

options.A: Arbitration, as provided in the General Conditions of Contract
options.B: Direct decision of the Railway Board
options.C: Reference to the State Government
options.D: Recovery from the security deposit without further process

e: The GCC contains an arbitration clause under which disputes that cannot be settled amicably between the Railway and the contractor are resolved through arbitration, whose award is binding on both parties.

q: In an EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) contract, the contractor is responsible for:

options.A: Only the detailed design of the project
options.B: Design and engineering, procurement of materials and construction of the project on a turnkey basis
options.C: Only the supply of materials
options.D: Maintenance of the asset after completion, for its entire life

e: In an EPC contract, the contractor bears single-point responsibility for design and engineering, procurement of materials and construction, delivering the project complete on a turnkey basis.

q: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is used for:

options.A: Inviting works tenders of zonal railways
options.B: Payment of salaries to railway staff
options.C: Online procurement of goods and services by government departments and organisations
options.D: Sale of scrap through e-auction

e: GeM is the online marketplace through which government departments and organisations procure goods and services; it is not used for inviting works tenders of zonal railways.

q: In a genuine emergency, tenders can be dispensed with and the work arranged without calling tenders on the basis of:

options.A: A verbal order of the sectional officer
options.B: A recorded urgency certificate by the competent authority
options.C: Approval of the tender committee after the work is done
options.D: The recommendation of the contractor already working in the section

e: In a genuine emergency, tenders may be dispensed with only on the strength of an urgency certificate recorded by the competent authority certifying the emergent nature of the work.

q: The 'D&G charges' levied in connection with works stand for:

options.A: Design and Geology charges
options.B: Departmental and General charges
options.C: Damage and Guarantee charges
options.D: Division and Group charges

e: D&G charges stand for Departmental and General charges, levied as a percentage on the cost of a work to cover the establishment and general overhead charges of the Railway.

q: Departmental charges are levied on deposit works in order to cover:

options.A: The profit margin of the Railways
options.B: The dividend payable to General Finances
options.C: The cost of establishment and tools and plant employed in executing and supervising the work
options.D: The cost of land acquisition

e: Departmental charges are levied on deposit works to recover the cost of the establishment and the tools and plant employed in executing and supervising the work on behalf of the outside body.

q: The List of Approved Works (LAW) forms part of:

options.A: The Pink Book containing the Works Programme of the Railways
options.B: The Indian Railway Financial Code
options.C: The annual Appropriation Accounts
options.D: The Audit Report of the C&AG

e: The List of Approved Works (LAW) forms part of the Pink Book, which contains the Works Programme of the Railways approved for the year under the various Plan Heads.

q: In connection with surveys for new railway lines, PETS stands for:

options.A: Preliminary Estimate and Traffic Statement
options.B: Project Evaluation and Technical Survey
options.C: Passenger Earnings and Traffic Survey
options.D: Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey

e: PETS stands for Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey, which is carried out for a proposed new line to examine its engineering feasibility and traffic prospects before further stages are taken up.

q: The role of the Finance member in a Tender Committee is primarily to:

options.A: Prepare the tender documents
options.B: Ensure that the tender is financially sound, funds are available and financial propriety is observed
options.C: Execute the work after award
options.D: Inspect the work during execution

e: The Finance member of a Tender Committee examines the financial soundness of the offers, ensures availability of funds and sees that financial propriety is observed before acceptance of a tender is recommended.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Concurrence is the formal prior agreement of the Finance branch to a proposal, without which the sanction is not complete.
2. Vetting means the detailed examination and checking of the figures of an estimate or proposal by Finance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: concurrence is the formal prior agreement of the Finance branch without which a sanction involving expenditure is not complete, and vetting is the detailed examination and checking of figures by Finance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Write-off means removing from the books an amount or an asset which is irrecoverable, with the sanction of the competent authority.
2. Write-back means crediting back a liability or provision which is no longer required.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: write-off removes an irrecoverable amount or useless asset from the books with the sanction of the competent authority, while write-back credits back a liability or provision no longer required.

q: One of the canons of financial propriety is that:

options.A: The amount of allowances granted to a government servant should be so regulated that the allowances are not, on the whole, a source of profit to the recipient
options.B: The entire budget allotment must be spent before the close of the financial year
options.C: A sanctioning authority may sanction expenditure from which it derives personal benefit
options.D: Estimates should always provide for amounts in excess of the actual requirement

e: One of the canons of financial propriety is that the allowances granted to a Government servant to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that, on the whole, they are not a source of profit to him.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure incurred from public funds should not be prima facie more than what the occasion demands.
2. Public funds should not be utilised for the benefit of a particular person or a section of the community unless the amount involved is infinitesimal or the claim could be enforced in a court of law.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are canons of financial propriety: expenditure from public funds should not exceed what the occasion demands, and public money should not benefit a particular person or section except in the exceptions stated.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of estimate prepared in connection with a railway work?

options.A: Abstract estimate
options.B: Detailed estimate
options.C: Running estimate
options.D: Supplementary estimate

e: Abstract, detailed and supplementary estimates are the recognised types of estimates for a work; there is no estimate called a running estimate - running bills relate to payment, not to an estimate.

q: An abstract estimate of a work is:

options.A: Prepared after the completion of the work
options.B: The basis on which the contractor's final bill is paid
options.C: Prepared only for deposit works
options.D: Prepared at the preliminary stage to arrive at the approximate cost of a proposed work before detailed investigations are completed

e: An abstract estimate is prepared at the preliminary stage and gives only the approximate cost of a proposed work, before detailed designs and investigations have been completed.

q: As a general rule, no work should be commenced unless:

options.A: A contractor has been informally selected for it
options.B: A detailed estimate for the work has been sanctioned and funds are available/allotted for it
options.C: Its completion report has been approved
options.D: The tender committee has been dispensed with

e: As a general rule, no work should be commenced unless a detailed estimate for it has been sanctioned and funds are available or allotted for it; starting work otherwise violates the basic rules of works expenditure.

q: A revised estimate is prepared when:

options.A: The cost of a sanctioned work is expected to exceed the sanctioned estimate materially, whether due to rise in prices or other causes
options.B: The work has been physically completed
options.C: The contractor applies for extra items of work
options.D: Surplus materials are returned to the stores depot

e: A revised estimate is prepared when the cost of a sanctioned work is expected to exceed the sanctioned estimate materially, whether due to rise in prices or other causes, so that revised sanction is obtained.

q: A supplementary estimate is prepared:

options.A: For obtaining the original sanction of a work
options.B: For additions or alterations found necessary during the execution of a work already sanctioned
options.C: For the annual maintenance of existing assets
options.D: For the purchase of stores items

e: A supplementary estimate is prepared for additions or alterations found necessary during the execution of a work already sanctioned, and is sanctioned in addition to the original estimate of the work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure.
2. Expenditure incurred in excess of the amount sanctioned is also treated as unsanctioned expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure, and expenditure incurred in excess of the sanctioned amount is likewise treated as unsanctioned.

q: Unsanctioned expenditure noticed in the accounts:

options.A: Is written off automatically at the end of the year
options.B: Is recovered from the contractor executing the work
options.C: Is ignored if the amount involved is small
options.D: Must be regularised under the orders of the competent authority and is brought to notice in the Appropriation Accounts

e: Unsanctioned expenditure must be regularised under the orders of the competent authority, and it is also brought to notice in the Appropriation Accounts for the information of Parliament.

q: Periodical Control over Capital Expenditure (COE) statements are intended to:

options.A: Record the attendance of engineering staff
options.B: Keep a watch over the progress of expenditure on capital works against sanctioned costs and allotments, so that excesses and overruns are noticed in time
options.C: Value the stores balances of depots
options.D: Prepare tender notices for works

e: Periodical COE statements keep a watch over the progress of expenditure on capital works against the sanctioned costs and allotments, so that excesses and cost overruns are noticed and controlled in time.

q: The normal method of inviting tenders for execution of railway works is:

options.A: Open tender
options.B: Single tender
options.C: Nomination
options.D: Verbal quotation

e: Open tender, invited through public advertisement, is the normal method of inviting tenders for railway works, as it gives equal opportunity to all eligible contractors and ensures competition.

q: Limited tenders are invited:

options.A: Through advertisement in newspapers from all intending contractors
options.B: From the general public
options.C: Only from government departments
options.D: From a restricted number of approved/empanelled contractors, generally for specialised requirements or where the open tender procedure is not practicable

e: Limited tenders are invited only from a restricted number of approved or empanelled contractors, a course adopted generally for specialised requirements or where the open tender procedure is not practicable.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Inviting a single tender is an exception to the normal open tender system and requires the approval of the competent authority, with the reasons recorded.
2. Single tender may be resorted to as a matter of routine to save time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: inviting a single tender is an exception to the normal open tender system and requires the approval of the competent authority with reasons recorded. Statement 2 is false, as it cannot be resorted to routinely merely to save time.

q: For works of small value, the formal tender system may be dispensed with and the work arranged on the basis of:

options.A: Verbal instructions of the sectional staff
options.B: Quotations obtained from contractors
options.C: Nomination by the contractor already working in the section
options.D: Advertisement in newspapers

e: For works of small value, the formal tender system may be dispensed with and the work arranged on the basis of quotations obtained from contractors, keeping the procedure proportionate to the value involved.

q: A tender committee constituted for examination of works tenders normally comprises:

options.A: The General Manager and the Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: Only the executive officer dealing with the work
options.C: The executive officer, the finance/accounts officer and an officer of another department
options.D: Representatives of the tenderers

e: A Tender Committee normally comprises the executive officer dealing with the work, the finance/accounts officer and an officer of another department, so that its recommendation is balanced and not of one officer alone.

q: 'Direct acceptance' of a tender means that:

options.A: The lowest tender is accepted automatically
options.B: The contractor conveys his acceptance of the work
options.C: The acceptance is conveyed verbally to the tenderer
options.D: The competent authority accepts the tender on its own without the recommendation of a tender committee, as permissible for tenders of low value

e: Direct acceptance means the competent authority accepts the tender on its own, within its powers, without the recommendation of a tender committee, a course permissible for tenders of low value.

q: The Earnest Money Deposit of a tenderer is liable to be forfeited when the tenderer:

options.A: Withdraws or modifies his tender within the period of validity, or having been awarded the work, fails to accept it or to sign the agreement
options.B: Does not happen to be the lowest tenderer
options.C: Seeks a clarification of the tender conditions
options.D: Submits his tender under the two-packet system

e: EMD is forfeited when a tenderer withdraws or modifies his tender within the period of its validity, or, having been awarded the work, fails to accept it or to sign the agreement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Earnest Money Deposit is furnished by the tenderers along with their tenders.
2. Security Deposit is also furnished by every tenderer along with his tender.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: EMD is furnished by tenderers along with their tenders. Statement 2 is false: Security Deposit is furnished only by the successful tenderer after award of the work, not by every tenderer.

q: The Performance Guarantee submitted by a contractor is released back to him:

options.A: Immediately on issue of the Letter of Acceptance
options.B: On payment of the first running bill
options.C: On the opening of tenders
options.D: After satisfactory completion of the work and fulfilment of the contract obligations, including the maintenance period where applicable

e: The Performance Guarantee is released only after the contractor has satisfactorily completed the work and fulfilled all contract obligations, including the maintenance period where applicable, since it secures performance till then.

q: The Security Deposit of a contractor is refunded:

options.A: As soon as the work is commenced
options.B: After successful completion of the work, settlement of the final bill and clearance of all dues and recoveries
options.C: On expiry of the validity of the tender
options.D: As soon as surplus materials are returned to the depot

e: The Security Deposit is refunded after the work is successfully completed, the final bill is settled and all dues and recoveries outstanding against the contractor are cleared.

q: A 'secured advance' in a works contract is an advance given to the contractor:

options.A: Against the materials brought by the contractor to the site of the work for incorporation in the work
options.B: For mobilising his establishment before starting the work
options.C: Against the wages payable to his labour
options.D: For purchase of tools and plant for the Railway

e: A secured advance is paid to the contractor against the materials brought by him to the site of the work for incorporation in the work, so that he is assisted with funds for materials actually at site.

q: On-account (running) payments made to a contractor during the progress of a work are based on:

options.A: The abstract estimate of the work
options.B: The contractor's own statement of work done
options.C: The measurements of work done recorded in the Measurement Book
options.D: The final bill of the work

e: On-account or running payments are made only for work actually done, on the basis of the measurements of work done recorded in the Measurement Book, and not on the contractor's own statement.

q: Where a contractor fails in or abandons the work and the contract is terminated, the Railway may get the remaining work executed:

options.A: Only after obtaining a decree of the court
options.B: Free of charge by another agency
options.C: By its own departmental staff in every case
options.D: At the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor

e: Where a contractor fails in or abandons the work and the contract is terminated, the Railway may get the remaining work executed by another agency at the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A works contract can be terminated for defaults of the contractor such as failure to start the work, abandonment of the work or persistent slow progress.
2. On such termination, the consequences, including forfeiture of the security deposit and performance guarantee, are decided by the contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: a works contract can be terminated for defaults such as failure to start the work, abandonment or persistent slow progress. Statement 2 is false, as the consequences on termination are decided by the Railway, not by the contractor.

q: Extension of the period of completion of a work can be granted to a contractor when the delay:

options.A: Is due to causes beyond the control of the contractor, such as the failure of the Railway to hand over the site or to supply departmental materials
options.B: Is entirely due to the neglect of the contractor
options.C: Is claimed by the contractor for any reason whatsoever, as a matter of right
options.D: Can never be granted under the General Conditions of Contract

e: Extension of the completion period is granted when the delay is due to causes beyond the control of the contractor, such as failure of the Railway to hand over the site or to supply departmental materials in time.

q: Defects which appear in a completed work during the maintenance/defect liability period are required to be:

options.A: Ignored until the work is taken up again for repairs
options.B: Made good by the contractor at his own cost
options.C: Repaired by the Railway at its own cost in all cases
options.D: Charged to the contractor's security deposit without any notice to him

e: Defects appearing in a completed work during the maintenance or defect liability period are required to be made good by the contractor at his own cost under the contract conditions.

q: In an item-rate works contract, the contractor is paid:

options.A: A lump sum for the whole work
options.B: On a cost-plus basis
options.C: At the rates given in the schedule of rates only
options.D: For the actual quantities of each item of work executed, at the rates quoted by him for those items

e: In an item-rate contract, the contractor is paid for the actual quantities of each item of work executed, at the rates quoted by him for those items, so the total depends on measured quantities.

q: In a lump-sum contract:

options.A: Every item of work is separately measured and paid for
options.B: The rates are revised every month with reference to price indices
options.C: The contractor undertakes only the supply of materials
options.D: The contractor agrees to execute the complete work, as defined in the contract, for a fixed lump-sum price

e: In a lump-sum contract, the contractor agrees to execute the complete work as defined in the contract for a fixed lump-sum price, without item-wise measurement and payment for each item.

q: IREPS (Indian Railways e-Procurement System) is used for:

options.A: Payment of pension to retired staff
options.B: Issue of privilege passes
options.C: Online tendering, including issue of tender notices and submission of bids for procurement
options.D: Booking of passenger tickets

e: IREPS, the Indian Railways e-Procurement System, is the portal used for online tendering, including issue of tender notices and submission of bids for procurement on the Railways.

q: Where the different documents forming part of a contract are at variance with one another, the matter is decided according to:

options.A: The preference of the contractor
options.B: The order of precedence of the documents as laid down in the contract conditions/General Conditions of Contract
options.C: The date of the oldest document
options.D: The discretion of the sectional staff

e: Where the documents forming part of a contract are at variance with one another, the matter is decided according to the order of precedence of the documents laid down in the contract conditions and the GCC.

q: In the BOOT model of project execution, the private partner:

options.A: Only finances the project
options.B: Only constructs the asset and hands it over immediately
options.C: Acts as the auditor of the project
options.D: Builds, Owns and Operates the asset during the concession period and Transfers it at the end of that period

e: In the BOOT model, the private partner Builds, Owns and Operates the asset during the concession period and Transfers it to the authority at the end of that period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is a separate entity or company created for the execution of a specific project.
2. Joint Venture companies have been formed by the Railways with State Governments for the development and execution of railway projects in the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: a Special Purpose Vehicle is a separate entity created for executing a specific project, and the Railways have formed Joint Venture companies with State Governments for development and execution of railway projects in the States.

q: Way-leave charges in connection with railway land are recovered for:

options.A: Permitting facilities such as pipelines, cables or roads to cross or run along railway land
options.B: Delay in completion of works by contractors
options.C: Use of railway rest houses by officers
options.D: Occupation of railway quarters by staff

e: Way-leave charges are recovered for permitting facilities such as pipelines, cables or roads to cross or run along railway land, without transferring any ownership of the land.

q: A Letter of Credit in contract transactions is:

options.A: A letter permitting the contractor to commence the work
options.B: An undertaking given by a bank, at the request of the purchaser, to make payment to the supplier on fulfilment of the conditions specified in the credit
options.C: A note recording a credit balance in the contractor's account
options.D: A licence issued for import of materials

e: A Letter of Credit is an undertaking given by a bank, at the request of the purchaser, to make payment to the supplier on fulfilment of the conditions specified in the credit.

q: Railway land is generally given for commercial purposes on licence rather than on lease, so that:

options.A: A higher rent can be charged from the user
options.B: The land becomes the property of the user in due course
options.C: The arrangement becomes permanent and irrevocable
options.D: The licensee acquires no ownership or tenancy rights over the land and the Railway can resume it on termination of the licence

e: Railway land is given on licence rather than lease so that the licensee acquires no ownership or tenancy rights over it and the Railway can resume the land on termination of the licence.

q: The Social Service Obligations of the Railways represent:

options.A: The expenditure on staff welfare functions
options.B: The cost of maintaining officers' clubs
options.C: The losses borne by the Railways on uneconomic services and facilities provided in the larger public interest, such as uneconomic branch lines and concessional fares
options.D: The expenditure on publicity through social media

e: Social Service Obligations represent the losses borne by the Railways on uneconomic services and facilities provided in the larger public interest, such as uneconomic branch lines and concessional fares.

q: Which of the following is a line-capacity augmentation work?

options.A: Painting of station buildings
options.B: Doubling of a single-line section and provision of additional crossing loops
options.C: Award of a catering contract
options.D: Printing of time tables

e: Doubling of a single-line section and provision of additional crossing loops directly increase the number of trains that can be run over the section, and are therefore line-capacity augmentation works.

q: The USSOR used in connection with railway works:

options.A: Contains the list of approved contractors
options.B: Fixes the fares chargeable from passengers
options.C: Contains the scales of departmental charges
options.D: Provides the unified standard schedule rates for items of work, used in preparing estimates and in analysing rates

e: The USSOR provides the unified standard schedule rates for items of work on the Railways and is used in preparing estimates and in analysing the rates quoted for works.

q: An 'imprest' in railway working is:

options.A: A deposit taken from contractors
options.B: A type of limited tender
options.C: A standing advance of a fixed amount placed at the disposal of an officer for meeting petty and day-to-day expenditure
options.D: A register of assets created

e: An imprest is a standing advance of a fixed amount placed at the disposal of an officer for meeting petty and day-to-day expenditure, avoiding repeated sanctions for small payments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An imprest is recouped from time to time on the basis of paid vouchers, so that the holder again has the full imprest amount at his disposal.
2. The holder of an imprest is required to maintain an account of the expenditure incurred out of it and to produce vouchers in support of the expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: an imprest is recouped from time to time on the basis of paid vouchers so that the full amount is again at the holder's disposal, and the holder must maintain an account of the expenditure with vouchers in support.

q: The cash book maintained in a railway cash office:

options.A: Records all receipts and payments of cash in chronological order, and its balance is tallied with the actual cash in hand
options.B: Records only the payments of salary to staff
options.C: Is maintained by the contractors executing works
options.D: Records the stores issued to works

e: The cash book records all receipts and payments of cash in chronological order, and its balance is tallied with the actual cash in hand to ensure correctness of the cash account.

q: The Contractor's Ledger maintained in the accounts office shows:

options.A: The leave account of the contractors
options.B: The list of contractors approved for works
options.C: The attendance of labour engaged by contractors
options.D: Contractor-wise details of bills passed, advances made, recoveries effected and the balance payable

e: The Contractor's Ledger maintained in the accounts office shows, contractor-wise, the bills passed, advances made, recoveries effected and the balance payable, giving a complete picture of each contractor's account.

q: A deposit work on behalf of an outside body is taken in hand by the Railway only after:

options.A: The completion report of the work is received
options.B: The estimated cost of the work, together with departmental charges, is deposited by the body concerned
options.C: The tenders for the work are opened
options.D: The work is entered in the Pink Book

e: A deposit work on behalf of an outside body is taken in hand only after the estimated cost of the work, together with departmental charges, is deposited by the body concerned.

q: A material modification of a sanctioned work requires:

options.A: Prior sanction of the competent authority, with finance concurrence, before the modified portion of the work is executed
options.B: Sanction only after the whole work is completed
options.C: The approval of the contractor executing the work
options.D: The approval of the Railway Board in every case, however small the modification

e: A material modification of a sanctioned work requires the prior sanction of the competent authority, with finance concurrence, before the modified portion of the work is executed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reconnaissance survey is the first stage of survey carried out for a proposed new railway line.
2. The detailed estimate for a new line is prepared after the final location survey has fixed the alignment on the ground.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: reconnaissance survey is the first stage of survey for a proposed new line, and the detailed estimate is prepared after the final location survey has fixed the alignment on the ground.

q: Administrative approval in connection with a railway work means:

options.A: The sanction of the detailed estimate by the Accounts branch
options.B: The approval in principle, by the competent authority, of the proposal to execute the work, accorded before its detailed estimate is prepared and sanctioned
options.C: The acceptance of the lowest tender for the work
options.D: The approval of the completion report of the work

e: Administrative approval is the approval in principle, by the competent authority, of the proposal to execute a work, and it is accorded before the detailed estimate of the work is prepared and sanctioned.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Technical sanction relates to the technical soundness of the design and of the detailed estimate of a work.
2. Expenditure sanction is the authority accorded by the competent authority permitting expenditure to be incurred on a work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: technical sanction relates to the technical soundness of the design and detailed estimate of a work, while expenditure sanction is the authority permitting expenditure to be incurred on the work.

q: Administrative approval of a new work is normally accorded on the basis of:

options.A: An abstract (preliminary) estimate accompanied by a report explaining the necessity and justification of the work
options.B: The final bill of a similar work executed earlier
options.C: The accepted tender of the contractor
options.D: The completion estimate of the work

e: Administrative approval of a new work is normally accorded on the basis of an abstract or preliminary estimate accompanied by a report explaining the necessity and justification of the work.

q: A detailed estimate of a work is prepared on the basis of:

options.A: Rough dimensions and lump-sum rates
options.B: The rates quoted by the lowest tenderer
options.C: The previous year's actual expenditure on similar works
options.D: Detailed designs, drawings and specifications, with the quantities of each item of work worked out and priced at the applicable rates

e: A detailed estimate is prepared on the basis of detailed designs, drawings and specifications, with the quantities of each item of work worked out and priced at the applicable rates.

q: The provision for 'contingencies' made in a detailed estimate is intended to cover:

options.A: The profit of the contractor
options.B: Petty and unforeseen items of expenditure which cannot be foreseen and specifically provided for in the estimate
options.C: The departmental charges of the work
options.D: Escalation of prices over the whole contract period

e: The provision for contingencies in a detailed estimate is intended to cover petty and unforeseen items of expenditure which cannot be foreseen and specifically provided for in the estimate.

q: Where the rate for an item of work is not available in the schedule of rates, it is worked out by 'analysis of rates', which takes into account:

options.A: Only the cost of labour for the item
options.B: The rates of the adjoining railway division, without any working
options.C: The average of the rates quoted by all the tenderers
options.D: The cost of materials, labour, carriage, tools and plant and other charges involved in executing the item

e: Where a schedule rate is not available, the rate is worked out by analysis of rates, taking into account the cost of materials, labour, carriage, tools and plant and other charges involved in executing the item.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of a detailed estimate?

options.A: Detailed drawings and designs
options.B: Item-wise calculation of quantities
options.C: The rates quoted by tenderers for the work
options.D: Analysis of rates for items not covered by the schedule of rates

e: A detailed estimate comprises detailed drawings and designs, item-wise calculation of quantities and analysis of rates for items not covered by the schedule of rates; the rates quoted by tenderers arise later at the tender stage and form no part of it.

q: An 'extra item' in a works contract is:

options.A: An item executed in place of an item originally provided in the contract
options.B: An item of work not included in the original contract, which is found necessary during execution and is ordered to be executed
options.C: An item for which the contractor quotes an abnormally high rate
options.D: An item of the schedule of rates which the contractor refuses to execute

e: An extra item is an item of work not included in the original contract which is found necessary during execution and is ordered to be executed as an addition to the contract.

q: A 'substituted item' in a works contract is:

options.A: An additional item ordered over and above the contract items
options.B: An item executed with materials supplied free by the Railway
options.C: An item whose rate is substituted by the tender committee
options.D: An item of work executed in place of an item originally provided in the contract, in lieu of it

e: A substituted item is an item of work executed in place of an item originally provided in the contract, in lieu of it, and not an additional item over and above the contract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An extra item is additional to the items provided in the original contract.
2. A substituted item replaces an item originally provided in the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: an extra item is additional to the items provided in the original contract, while a substituted item replaces an item originally provided in the contract.

q: The variations between the provisions of the sanctioned estimate and the work as actually executed are explained, at the completion stage, in:

options.A: A deviation statement accompanying the completion estimate/report
options.B: The tender notice inviting tenders for the work
options.C: The contractor's final bill
options.D: The urgency certificate for the work

e: The variations between the provisions of the sanctioned estimate and the work as actually executed are explained at the completion stage in a deviation statement accompanying the completion estimate or report.

q: A completion estimate of a work is prepared:

options.A: At the proposal stage, before administrative approval
options.B: When the work is nearing completion, so as to arrive at the final cost of the work as executed and obtain sanction for it where necessary
options.C: For inviting tenders for the work
options.D: Only when the asset created by the work is disposed of

e: A completion estimate is prepared when the work is nearing completion, so as to arrive at the final cost of the work as executed and to obtain sanction for it where necessary.

q: A mobilisation advance in a works contract is:

options.A: An advance against materials brought by the contractor to the site of the work
options.B: A loan given to the contractor for purchasing land for the work
options.C: The final payment made to the contractor after completion of the work
options.D: An advance paid to the contractor at the commencement of the work to enable him to mobilise men, materials and equipment for starting the work

e: A mobilisation advance is paid to the contractor at the commencement of the work to enable him to mobilise men, materials and equipment for starting the work; it is distinct from a secured advance against materials.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mobilisation advance is paid at the commencement of the work to enable the contractor to mobilise his resources for the work.
2. Mobilisation advance is recovered from the contractor's subsequent on-account (running) bills.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: mobilisation advance is paid at the commencement of the work to enable the contractor to mobilise his resources, and it is recovered from his subsequent on-account or running bills.

q: An advance against plant and machinery in a works contract is granted:

options.A: Against new plant and machinery brought by the contractor to the site for use on the work
options.B: Against the contractor's office furniture
options.C: For purchase of vehicles for the Railway
options.D: Only after the completion of the work

e: An advance against plant and machinery is granted against new plant and machinery brought by the contractor to the site for use on the work.

q: The financial powers of railway officers for sanctioning works and accepting tenders are laid down in:

options.A: The Railways Act, 1989
options.B: The Schedule of Powers
options.C: The General Financial Rules only
options.D: The annual Pink Book

e: The financial powers of railway officers for sanctioning works and accepting tenders are laid down in the Schedule of Powers, which prescribes the limits within which each officer may exercise such powers.

q: A work which is beyond the powers of sanction of the General Manager requires the sanction of:

options.A: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: The Chief Engineer of the zone
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The Finance Secretary of the State Government

e: A work which is beyond the powers of sanction of the General Manager requires the sanction of the Railway Board, the highest authority for sanctioning railway works.

q: The 'negative powers' of a General Manager refer to:

options.A: Powers to cancel any tender at any stage
options.B: Powers exercised by the General Manager only during emergencies
options.C: Powers delegated by the General Manager to officers under him
options.D: Matters which the General Manager is specifically not competent to sanction, and which must be referred to the Railway Board notwithstanding his general powers

e: Negative powers are matters which the General Manager is specifically not competent to sanction; notwithstanding his general powers, such matters must be referred to the Railway Board.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) was created to finance:

options.A: Safety-related works, such as renewal and replacement of track, signalling and other safety assets
options.B: Construction of staff quarters
options.C: Catering and tourism projects
options.D: Manufacture of passenger coaches

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) was created to finance safety-related works, such as renewal and replacement of track, signalling and other safety assets.

q: The Railway Safety Fund (RSF) is used mainly for works connected with:

options.A: Doubling of busy main lines
options.B: Safety at level crossings, such as construction of road over-bridges/road under-bridges and other level-crossing safety works
options.C: Electrification of branch lines
options.D: Development of freight terminals

e: The Railway Safety Fund (RSF) is used mainly for works connected with safety at level crossings, such as construction of road over-bridges and road under-bridges and other level-crossing safety works.

q: Track renewals on the Railways are normally financed from:

options.A: Capital
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF)
options.D: Revenue (working expenses)

e: Track renewals replace worn-out assets and are normally financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF), which is provided for renewal and replacement of assets on the Railways.

q: The amount deposited by an outside body for execution of a deposit work is credited:

options.A: To the earnings of the Railway
options.B: To the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Directly to the contractor's account
options.D: To a deposit head of account (under Deposits in the Public Account), against which the expenditure on the work is booked

e: The amount deposited by an outside body for a deposit work is credited to a deposit head of account under Deposits in the Public Account, and the expenditure on the work is booked against that deposit.

q: If, during execution, the cost of a deposit work is likely to exceed the amount deposited by the party:

options.A: The party should be called upon to deposit the additional amount required, and expenditure beyond the deposit should not be incurred in anticipation of it
options.B: The excess is automatically borne by the Railways
options.C: The contractor is asked to bear the excess
options.D: The excess is adjusted against the departmental charges of another work

e: If the cost of a deposit work is likely to exceed the amount deposited, the party should be called upon to deposit the additional amount required, and expenditure beyond the deposit should not be incurred in anticipation of it.

q: 'Agency charges' in connection with a work are payable when:

options.A: The work is executed departmentally by the Railway's own staff
options.B: The contractor engages an agent for obtaining materials
options.C: The work is executed through another agency, such as another government department or a public sector undertaking, on behalf of the Railway, to cover that agency's establishment and supervision costs
options.D: The tender is accepted directly without a tender committee

e: Agency charges are payable when a work is executed through another agency, such as another government department or a public sector undertaking, on behalf of the Railway, to cover that agency's establishment and supervision costs.

q: The departmental/agency charges levied on works are also commonly known as:

options.A: Liquidated charges
options.B: Centage charges, being levied as a percentage of the cost of the work
options.C: Suspense charges
options.D: Book charges

e: The departmental and agency charges levied on works are commonly known as centage charges because they are levied as a percentage of the cost of the work.
